why: Drawing 3349 shows a plain waistband with no side-adjuster hardware and a single side belt loop; the photo navy waistband is likewise bare of any buckle, strap or tab and carries one plain loop, so the no-adjuster construction matches.

The red marker in the drawing outlines a strap-and-buckle adjuster set into the waistband; the photo shows exactly that - a metal D-frame buckle on a hexagonal fabric strap - with a belt loop sitting immediately beside it, matching buckle WITH belt loop.

Drawing 3330 marks evenly spaced single narrow loops around the waistband; the photo shows about six narrow single-strip loops evenly distributed across the visible front/side wrap, consistent with a full seven-loop set, and the loops are single rather than doubled or wide.

Drawing 3329 has a completely clean waistband with no loop markers at all; the photographed navy waistband likewise carries zero belt loops across its entire visible span, only a smooth top edge and pleated front, so No Belt Loops is faithfully depicted.

Drawing 3331 Double marks wide split blocks rather than the narrow single bars used on the Regular drawing; the photo left loop resolves into two narrow parallel straps with separate bartacks sitting side by side, matching the paired passant construction described for this option.

Drawing 3332 uses noticeably wider outlined loop markers than the Regular 3330 drawing; the photographed loops are single strips roughly twice the width of those in loops-standard.webp under the same crop, consistent with the 2.0 cm wide-loop spec.

Drawing 3618 places a single red loop marker on the waistband at the wearer right front and nowhere else; the photo shows exactly one belt loop, positioned left of the fly from the viewer side, with the rest of the waistband bare.

Drawing 333E marks two red X shapes symmetrically flanking the centre-front fly; the photo shows two crossed-strap X loops in the same mirrored positions either side of the fly, matching both the crossed geometry and the count of two front X positions.

The back-view drawing marks a tab spanning the centre-back waistband with a buckle at its midpoint and no buttons; the photo shows a back waistband tab straddling the centre-back seam closed by a metal square-frame buckle, with two besom back pockets below, matching the buckle-not-buttons construction.

The drawing shows a pointed hexagonal centre-back tab with four small buttons drawn across the waistband; the photo reproduces the pointed hexagonal tab at centre back with exactly four buttons in the same inner-pair plus outer-pair arrangement, matching the four-buttons spec.

Drawing 302M only distinguishing feature is one red dart line dropping from the waistband on each front panel, but the photo shows a completely smooth dartless flat front - visually indistinguishable from the separate Flat Front (No Dart) option image, while the paired double-dart photo shot in the identical style renders its darts plainly, so the dart count is 0 instead of 1.

Drawing 302Y marks two short parallel dart lines per front panel below the waistband; the photo shows two tapering stitched folds on each side of the fly in matching mirrored positions that fade out a few inches down, with no open pleat, matching the flat-front double-dart count and placement.
